scenario: A cheerful boxy plant-cell character with a double-outlined wall and a happy face, its open front showing one huge smiling water-balloon vacuole squishing chloroplast friends (green lenses with pancake-disc stacks), a sleepy nucleus and a tiny mitochondrion against the wall; a watering can tips in from the top edge pouring big drops, one caught by a mitten hand; neighbour cells' double-lined walls peek in cut off by the left, right and bottom edges.
prompt:
A black-and-white CHILDREN'S COLORING BOOK page, square 1:1, 1080x1080. Composition must be SQUARE, never wide or landscape.

CRITICAL — READ FIRST: (a) the drawing must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES with NO frame, NO border line, NO box and NO white margin band; (b) there must be NO starburst, no radiating burst, no sparkle rays, no sunbeam rays and no sun with rays anywhere in the picture; (c) use a ZOOMED-IN composition where the main character and the background props all run past every edge of the square, so nothing floats in empty white space.

SCENE: A cheerful cartoon PLANT CELL character — a friendly little house-of-the-plant — fills almost the whole frame, zoomed in so close that its outer wall runs past the left, right and bottom edges of the picture.
- The PLANT CELL CHARACTER is one big, chunky ROUNDED RECTANGLE drawn with a DOUBLE OUTLINE (two parallel lines close together — its sturdy brick-like cell wall), tilted at a slight friendly angle. On the upper part of the wall band sits a big round happy face: two large round eyes with pupils, cheerful eyebrows and a wide open smile, plus two short stubby cartoon arms with mitten hands sticking out from the sides of the box.
- The front of the box is open like a big window, showing the cozy inside: ONE HUGE round WATER-BALLOON character — the central vacuole — takes up most of the room inside, drawn as a big plump balloon with a tiny peaceful smiling face and a little tied knot at the bottom; it is so big it gently squishes everything else against the inside of the wall.
- Squeezed into the space between the balloon and the wall: three or four little CHLOROPLAST friends — chunky green-bean / lens shapes, each with a simple happy face and a small stack of three plain pancake-discs drawn inside its body — and one round NUCLEUS character tucked into a corner, a simple circle fellow with a smaller circle (its nucleolus) as a button belly and a sleepy contented smile. One tiny bean-shaped mitochondrion friend with a squiggly curtain inside waves from another corner.
- From the top edge of the picture a big cartoon WATERING CAN tips in, partly cut off by the top edge, pouring a stream of large, simple, well-separated water DROPS down toward the plant cell character; one mitten hand reaches up happily to catch a drop. The drops are plain rounded teardrop shapes, each fully closed, no rays or splashes.
- BACKGROUND, filling the rest and running off the edges: the double-line walls of two or three NEIGHBOUR plant cells, drawn as partial rounded rectangles cut off by the left, right and bottom edges, each with a little chloroplast friend or a small balloon peeking inside; a few plain round bubbles floating in the gaps. Everything is CUT OFF by the image edges themselves.
- Everything is drawn LARGE, SIMPLE and CHUNKY, with generous open white areas inside every shape so a child can colour them in.

STYLE — coloring book line art:
- BOLD, THICK, EVEN BLACK OUTLINES on pure WHITE. Every shape fully closed.
- ABSOLUTELY NO shading, NO grey tones, NO hatching, NO stippling, NO cross-hatching, NO gradients, NO colour fill, NO solid black areas anywhere (eyes may have a small solid pupil only).
- Simple, cheerful, chunky cartoon shapes with plenty of white space.

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN — the page is rejected if any of these appear:
- ANY decorative STARBURST, comic-style radiating burst, "pow"/impact star, sparkle burst, twinkle burst, sun with rays, sunbeam rays, radiating speed lines, motion rays or halo of rays behind, around or under any character. NO radiating lines of any kind anywhere.
- ANY rectangle, square box outline, picture frame, panel edge, comic panel, border line, outer margin line, ground-line box, shelf, table, counter or vignette AROUND THE WHOLE PICTURE. The drawing must NOT sit inside a box of any kind. Do NOT draw a thin black line along or near the edge of the image. There must be NO white margin between the artwork and the image edge. (The plant cell character itself is a rounded box — that is correct — but it must run past the edges, never sit neatly inside them.)
- The artwork must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES of the square — the watering can is cut off by the top edge, and the neighbour cells' walls are cut off by the left, right and bottom edges.
- NO text, letters, numbers, words, captions, labels or watermarks anywhere.
- NO speech bubble, thought bubble or balloon of any kind (one is added separately afterwards).
- NO human figures, no real flames, no arrows.
